subject: Geo activation grace period & acceptable data-loss window
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@irisbank.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request — geo activation grace & RTO/RPO tolerance

Hi Stephanie / Naomi,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, IrisBank is preparing for a phased multi-region cutover in Q3 and we need to lock down the operational commitments for failover activation. Two items we need Redwood to confirm or carve out:

1) Activation grace window: We expect a short manual warm-standby activation window during which our on-call team will accept traffic to the secondary region. Can Redwood agree to a 30-minute activation grace (i.e., no SLA penalty for the first 30 minutes post-activation) while we validate connectivity and run smoke checks?

2) RTO/RPO sensitivity: For our tiered payments service, the bank can tolerate up to 3 minutes RTO but requires RPO to be no more than 60 seconds for transaction state. If you cannot meet RPO in certain edge scenarios (large KV-cache warmup after region switch), can Redwood document the expected data-loss profile and propose mitigation (incremental replay, temporary queueing)?

We attached our internal DR matrix for context. We also need to understand whether exceptions will be visible on the public status page or captured as a private incident with SLAs unaffected.

Goal: get a short written carveout we can present to our risk committee next week.

Appreciate a concise response with proposed language.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Reliability | IrisBank

Attachment: iris_dr_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet — DR targets by service)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@irisbank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — geo activation grace & RTO/RPO tolerance

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the matrix. We can work with this, but need to be explicit about two items:

- Activation grace: Redwood is open to a documented 30-minute grace window for the first activation event per planned switchover, provided the activation is initiated via our documented runbook and a Redwood on-call engineer is on the bridge. During that 30-minute window we will prioritize safety over availability (no SLA credit applied), and we will provide play-by-play logs to IrisBank.

- RPO guarantee: Our standard multi-region RPO for transaction surfaces is 0–30s for warm-standby patterns where prefix/KV caching can be primed. However, for cold-start failovers (e.g., upstream cache loss or cross-region storage lag) RPO cannot be guaranteed below 120s. For IrisBank's requirement of <=60s, we can offer an engineered mitigation: a short-lived write-ahead queue and accelerated pre-warm for transaction shards that reduces expected RPO to ~45–75s depending on concurrency. This will require a configuration change and an agreed testing window.

I've attached proposed SLA amendment language that captures the grace window and the conditional RPO carveout. High level next steps:
1) Naomi — can you review compliance language and flag anything we cannot accept?
2) Karthik — confirm whether the mitigation requires additional reserved capacity or different autoscaling triggers.
3) Daniel — please confirm whether IrisBank will accept (a) one activation grace per planned switchover, or (b) grace per calendar quarter.

If we align on wording, we'll route a short DocuSign amendment and record the exception on the private contract addenda (not public status page).

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Success, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-sla-amendment.docx

Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request — geo activation grace & RTO/RPO tolerance

Stephanie / Karthik — quick compliance review:

- Private incident vs public status: We should keep this as a private contract addendum tied to the IrisBank account. Anything that materially changes public uptime commitments must go through the SRE & legal review gate; this request is fine as a private carveout so long as we limit scope (per-service, per-activation) and log all activations in our audit trail.

- Data-loss / RPO language: The proposed-sla-amendment.docx needs a short section describing the failure modes that would cause the increased RPO (e.g., cross-region storage replication lag, KV cache cold start). Include a required post-incident tech memo from IrisBank summarizing lost transactions and reconciliation plan. That memo will be a gating artifact for renewal risk assessment.

- Security note: If we enable write-ahead queuing, ensure KMS policy is aligned and the queue retention is limited (30 days). Please include KMS key rotation windows in the exec summary.

I can draft a compliance paragraph to insert; tagging Legal is recommended before final DocuSign.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Risk & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Hi Daniel — circling back with agreed next steps and proposed contract language summary. Thank you all for the quick turnaround.

Summary (short form):
- Activation grace: one 30-minute grace window for each planned warm-standby activation. Redwood on-call must be engaged and runbook steps executed. No SLA credit during the grace window; incident will be recorded on IrisBank's private addenda.
- RPO: Default warm-standby RPO: 0–30s (when pre-warmed). Carveout: cold-start scenarios may experience up to 120s RPO. Agreed mitigation: optional write-ahead queue + accelerated pre-warm that targets 45–75s RPO. Mitigation requires a configuration rollout and a 2-week joint test.
- Compliance additions: Redwood to maintain KMS controls and 30-day queue retention; IrisBank to provide post-activation reconciliation memo for any data-loss event.

Next steps:
1) IrisBank: confirm whether you want the grace window per activation or quarterly by EOD Mon 4/23.
2) Redwood (Karthik): assess capacity/ops impact and estimate cost delta for the queue/pre-warm option by Tue 4/24.
3) Naomi: will draft one paragraph for compliance to embed; Stephanie will route for Legal review.

I'll open a HubSpot note and add the amendment to DocuSign once we have the activation cadence. DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABCDEF123456. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/987654.

Thanks — let's get this into a one-page addendum so IrisBank's risk committee can review next week.

Best,
